explanation: Shrunk scenario shows bodies 1 (10.5 Msun) and 3 (5.09 Msun) undergo a very close encounter: distance falls from 0.85 at step 24 to 0.48 at step 25 to 0.14 at step 26 (< 0.3 softening length). Substeps remain fixed at 6 despite rising accelerations, so the fixed-dt leapfrog integration becomes inaccurate: kinetic energy spikes from ~354 to ~493 while softened potential drops from ~-352 to ~-584 between steps 25-26, causing total energy to jump from +2.0 to -91.0 (change ~88.7, allowed ~21.6). Reducing dt to 0.005 with identical initial conditions and 26 steps eliminates the violation (energy change ~0.000058), proving the failure is due to insufficient time resolution / substep adaptation during the close approach.
vision_note: Two central bodies move toward each other across steps 23-25, their separation shrinking until they are almost touching in step 25. In step 26 they overlap as a single merged dot, showing an extremely close encounter well inside the normal spacing.
